question: If A and B are mutually exclusive, the general addition rule is:

options.text: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) + P(A ∩ B)

solution:
The correct answer is** P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mutually exclusive events** have no elements in common and cannot occur simultaneously.
 
• The union of two mutually exclusive events is the sum of their individual probabilities.
 
• The union of two events, A and B, is the event that either A or B occurs, or both occur. It is denoted as A ∪ B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **probability of a union **of events is equal to the sum of the probabilities of the individual events, as long as the events are mutually exclusive.
 
• It is important to determine if events are mutually exclusive before applying the addition rule.
 
• The addition rule for mutually exclusive events is a fundamental rule in probability theory and is widely used in various applications.
